content:
If you're a heavy user of the Apple Watch beta this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps are unable to open on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

These updates are rolling out via the App Store, with a "What's New" note reading: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27, with no new features added."

Apple notified developers this week that the process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and all other new operating systems) is expected to officially launch to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates have been pushed out in advance.

Apple said the fix is required due to issues with the arm64 segment in some watchOS apps. It appears they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging the apps to fix binary file compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue working without developers needing to take any action.
